# Implementation Accelerator Proposal

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments (fictional)
**Program:** Implementation Accelerator, AI Governance Academy
**Source:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with about 1,100 staff. Its AI footprint has three parts:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that the Client has no inventory of AI systems. The stated regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. The Client intends to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, and the start date is not yet fixed.

You stated the governing objective directly: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Three constraints shape the work:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 quality management system.

## 2. Why an Intensive AIMS Foundation Build Fits Now

**Decision timeline.** A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. The Accelerator could therefore run early in 2027, which leaves time before the Q2 2027 production target to adopt artifacts, assign owners and act on priorities. A longer discovery-led engagement would use more of that window before producing anything the Client can adopt.

**The audit finding.** The June 2026 finding names a specific gap: no AI system inventory. Day 2 of the Accelerator produces that inventory, seeded with the three known use cases. It is built so internal audit can trace it to a governance charter, a classification scheme and a risk register.

**Certification target.** ISO/IEC 42001 work is planned for next year. The Accelerator structures every artifact for future conformity work, so that work starts from adopted foundations rather than a blank page. This is readiness work. The Accelerator does not promise ISO/IEC 42001 certification or any audit result.

**Existing management systems.** Every artifact is designed to attach to the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and the ISO 9001 quality management system rather than stand alone. The Profile Block does not name the specific registers, procedures or records inside those systems, so each attachment point is `Unknown` until the Client identifies it on Day 1. The framework names alone are not taken as evidence that any particular register, process, control or record exists.

**Budget.** The US$25,000 price sits within the stated approval of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## 3. The Five-Day Build Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

The sequence follows two dependencies: the charter comes before policies, and the inventory comes before the risk register.

| Day | Build focus | Tailoring for Tamarack Instruments |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Governance charter and roles | Define purpose, scope, roles, decision rights and meeting cadence across the General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data and German plant manager roles. Identify attachment points in the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and ISO 9001 quality management system (currently `Unknown`). Record the works council consultation requirement as a governance gate. |
| 2 | AI system inventory and classification | Build the inventory schema and enter the chatbot, the visual inspection pilot and the planned sales forecasting system as first entries. Add classification fields oriented to the EU AI Act. Classification outcomes are orientation only: confirm with external counsel. System owners and system details not stated in the Profile Block are `Unknown`. |
| 3 | Risk and impact assessment plus risk register | Assess the inventoried systems and seed the risk register. Draft risk statements are grounded in the three use cases and the June 2026 audit finding, and are labeled as drafts for Client validation. GDPR and EU data residency considerations are captured where a system processes customer data. Which systems do so is `Unknown` until the Client confirms. |
| 4 | Core policies and operating procedures | Outline acceptable use, lifecycle governance, vendor and supplier governance, incident response and change management policies. Each is designed to attach to the existing management systems, with attachment points `Unknown` until confirmed. Items with legal effect: confirm with external counsel. |
| 5 | Evidence model, implementation priorities and executive readout | Map each artifact to the assurance question it answers, in a form useful to internal audit and to future ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work. Prioritize actions against the Q2 2027 production target. Deliver the executive readout. |

**Frameworks applied:**

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) structures the governance, risk and evidence artifacts.
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) structures the operating discipline behind them.
- AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) is the reference for the executive and board layer.

**Principles:** the work is guided by three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

## 4. Artifacts the Client Owns at Close

Each artifact leaves the week with a status of draft, reviewed or adopted. Adoption decisions remain with the Client.

1. AI governance charter, covering purpose, scope, roles, decision rights and meeting cadence
2. Roles and decision rights matrix
3. AI system inventory, with the three known use cases as first entries
4. AI system classification scheme, oriented to the EU AI Act (confirm with external counsel)
5. Risk and impact assessment method
6. AI risk register, with seeded draft risk statements for Client validation
7. Acceptable use policy outline
8. AI lifecycle governance policy outline
9. Vendor and supplier governance policy outline
10. AI incident response policy outline
11. AI change management policy outline
12. Core operating procedures supporting the policies above
13. Evidence model and evidence index
14. Prioritized implementation plan aligned to the Q2 2027 production target
15. Executive readout pack

- **Works council:** Where Accelerator outputs would touch production staff, the stated requirement to consult the German works council applies before implementation. The current consultation status is `Unknown`.
